[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Extended Events (XEvents) for Deep Diagnostics in Microsoft SQL Server"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to Extended Events"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"SQL Server Extended Events (XEvents) is a lightweight, highly scalable tracing and performance monitoring architecture. It replaces the legacy SQL Trace and SQL Server Profiler tools by utilizing vastly fewer system resources while offering granular insights into the Database Engine."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Concepts: Events, Targets, and Actions"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Events: Points of interest within the execution path of the SQL Server engine, such as lock acquisitions or query completions."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Targets: Consumers of events. Common targets include the ring buffer (in-memory) and the event file (disk)."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Actions: Additions to events that provide supplementary data, such as capturing the current T-SQL stack or call stack when an event fires."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Diagnostic Extended Event Session"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"The following T-SQL script creates an Extended Event session designed to capture queries that run longer than one second, including their actual execution plans and text."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"CREATE EVENT SESSION [Deep_Diagnostics] ON SERVER 
ADD EVENT sqlserver.sql_statement_completed(
    ACTION(sqlserver.sql_text, sqlserver.client_app_name, sqlserver.session_id)
    WHERE (duration > 1000000)
),
ADD EVENT sqlserver.rpc_completed(
    ACTION(sqlserver.sql_text, sqlserver.client_app_name, sqlserver.session_id)
    WHERE (duration > 1000000)
)
ADD TARGET package0.event_file(SET filename=N'Deep_Diagnostics.xel')
WITH (MAX_MEMORY=4096 KB, EVENT_RETENTION_MODE=ALLOW_SINGLE_EVENT_LOSS, MAX_DISPATCH_LATENCY=5 SECONDS);
GO"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Starting and Managing the Session"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the session is created, it must be explicitly started. You can also configure it to start automatically whenever SQL Server restarts by utilizing the startup state option."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"-- Start the session
ALTER EVENT SESSION [Deep_Diagnostics] ON SERVER STATE = START;

-- Stop the session
ALTER EVENT SESSION [Deep_Diagnostics] ON SERVER STATE = STOP;"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Querying Extended Event Data"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Instead of using the legacy Profiler interface, you can parse the target file directly using XML functions within T-SQL to analyze your captured diagnostics."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"SELECT 
    c.value('(event/@name)[1]', 'varchar(50)') AS event_name,
    c.value('(event/data[@name="duration"]/value)[1]', 'bigint') AS duration_microsec,
    c.value('(event/action[@name="sql_text"]/value)[1]', 'varchar(max)') AS sql_text,
    c.value('(event/action[@name="session_id"]/value)[1]', 'int') AS session_id
FROM (
    SELECT CAST(event_data AS XML) AS target_data
    FROM sys.fn_xe_file_target_read_file('Deep_Diagnostics*.xel', 'Deep_Diagnostics*.xem', NULL, NULL)
) as tab
CROSS APPLY target_data.nodes('//event') AS q(c);"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Extended Events provide a highly optimized framework for deep diagnostics in Microsoft SQL Server. By mastering custom sessions, filtering predicates, and target analysis, DBAs can isolate performance bottlenecks with minimal overhead."}]
